clue.text: In prison camp little one is a slow grower

parts.note: a stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp
a mite is a tiny creature or a small child

explanation.surface: A small inmate of a prison camp is slow to grow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a slow grower' is the definition: a cave formation that builds up drop by drop over centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Formations rising from cave floors accumulate mineral deposits extremely slowly, over thousands of years.

clue.text: Native born girl is outside

indicators.note: the girl is outside the other letter, wrapping round it

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl born locally is out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native born' reads as one phrase, but 'born' gives B, which goes inside SARA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabra is a Jew born in Israel, a native rather than an immigrant.

clue.text: He wants to pull down a ranch — it's in a mess

indicators.note: the words a ranch it's are in a mess, scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man wants to demolish a ranch that has fallen into disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pull down' of the definition means overthrowing the established order, not demolishing a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolutionary wants to tear down government and all established authority.

clue.text: Falls here exhausted western sterling arrangement

parts.note: all in means exhausted, worn out

indicators.note: an arrangement of the word sterling puts its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Exhausted, someone drops at a Western pound-sterling deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like a verb, but a fall is a scoring pin in wrestling.
explanation.definitionFit: In this freestyle sport a contestant scores by pinning the opponent's shoulders, a fall.

clue.text: Strange rise and fall in cattle plague

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the word for strange is read upwards

parts.note: rum means strange, odd
rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: An odd fluctuation is seen in an outbreak of disease among cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise and fall' looks like a fluctuation, but 'rise' turns RUM (strange) upwards to MUR, and 'fall' is RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Murrain is an old name for an infectious disease among livestock, an epizootic.

clue.text: Barman, a judge of wine, kept port originally

indicators.note: the judge of wine keeps the other letter inside

parts.note: a taster judges wine by tasting it

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of port

explanation.surface: A barman who judges wine has kept back some port.
explanation.walkthrough: P, the first letter of 'port', goes inside TASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster draws beer or other drinks from a tap, serving at a bar.

clue.text: Tea, say, laid outside — let it stand

indicators.note: laid is placed outside, so its letters go round the other piece

parts.note: laid means set, as a table is set

indicators.note: say signals that the word tea is taken by its sound, the name of a letter

parts.note: the drink tea sounds like the letter T

explanation.surface: Tea things are laid out on the table, and someone says to leave them there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you to hear 'Tea' as the letter T, which goes inside SET (laid).
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin proofreading mark tells the printer to ignore a correction and keep the original text.

clue.text: Junk food?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk food' reads as fast food; split it into worthless rubbish and an item of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe means nonsense or rubbish; it is also the stomach lining of cattle, eaten as offal.

clue.text: Handle intended, say, for physiotherapy

parts.note: to treat someone is to handle them

indicators.note: say signals that intended is taken by its sound

parts.note: intended means meant

explanation.surface: A physiotherapist means to handle you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you to hear MEANT (intended) as a sound, written MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Physiotherapy is a form of medical care given to a patient.

clue.text: As good an address as Seven Dials for heart-throbs (G&S)

definitions.text: As good an address as Seven Dials for heart-throbs (G&S)

parts.words: As good an address as Seven Dials for heart-throbs (G&S)
parts.note: Gilbert and Sullivan's Iolanthe says hearts beat as pure in a smart London square as in the slum of Seven Dials

explanation.surface: A fashionable address that, in an operetta, is as good for romance as a slum.
explanation.walkthrough: Seven Dials was a notorious London slum; Iolanthe pairs it with an aristocratic Belgravia square as equal homes for true hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand square in London's wealthy Belgravia district, named in Iolanthe.

clue.text: Fighter is king in 14 ac

indicators.note: the king is put in the other word, its letters split around it

parts.note: the answer to 14 across is crier, and a crier is a bawler
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A boxer who is king of the ring among town criers.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 across is CRIER; another word for one who cries is BAWLER, and R (king) goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawler is someone who fights noisily, a scrapper or street fighter.

clue.text: Abstract by egghead is clear-cut

parts.note: an abstract is a summary, a précis
the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: An intellectual's summary is sharply defined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but is read as the head (first letter) of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exact and sharply defined, with no vagueness, is clear-cut.

clue.text: Influential, like stock phrases about death

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons

indicators.note: stock phrases go about death, so its letters are wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: cant is hackneyed, insincere language
an end is a death

explanation.surface: An influential person relies on clichés when discussing mortality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like stock phrases' reads as describing the influential person, but 'like' just gives a short word and 'stock phrases' is hackneyed jargon; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the ascendant means being in a position of rising power and dominance.

clue.text: Welcome cry

explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish sense of 'greet' (to weep) is the less familiar half.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet is to welcome someone; in Scots, greet also means to weep or cry.

clue.text: Town's publicity officer in tears

explanation.walkthrough: A town crier walked the streets shouting news and notices, a traditional British civic role.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier proclaimed public announcements; someone in tears is weeping, one who cries.

clue.text: About a penny still unspent, with due respect

parts.note: c stands for circa, about
money in hand is still available, not yet spent

explanation.surface: Someone still has about a penny left to spend, politely.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa, about), A, P (penny) and IN HAND (unspent) run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming humbly, as a petitioner holding their hat, means showing deference.

clue.text: Countryman holding a, pair of kings is telling a story

indicators.note: the countryman holds the other letters inside him

parts.note: a native is a countryman, someone born in the country
R stands for Rex, king, so two kings make two Rs

explanation.surface: A local man with two monarchs in his hand spins a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of kings' suggests a poker hand, but each king is just R (Rex); the inserted letters go after the countryman's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something narrative recounts events in sequence, the way a tale or account does.

clue.text: Produce first class stencil set

indicators.note: produce means make something new, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: Make a top-quality stencil set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal: AI (A1, first class) plus STENCIL is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rigid that will not stretch or give is fixed, set firm.

clue.text: Element needs changing as MOT is up

indicators.note: the words as MOT is up must be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A car's roadworthiness test is due, so the element needs replacing.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the UK's annual roadworthiness test for cars; here its letters are just fodder for 'needs changing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft reactive alkali metal, chemical symbol K, is one of the chemical elements.

clue.text: Invest in a theatre seat

parts.note: a stall is a seat on the ground floor of a theatre

explanation.surface: Put money into a seat at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' suggests money, but it means formally placing someone in office. The stalls are the ground-floor seats in a British theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone is to install them formally in an office or rank.

clue.text: Old Scottish landowner underwrites State gas

indicators.note: underwrites means is written under, so in a down clue the landowner goes below

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for the US state of Maine
a thane was a Scottish lord holding land from the king

explanation.surface: An old Scottish laird guarantees a state's gas supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underwrites' suggests insurance, but it means THANE is written under ME in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is a flammable hydrocarbon, the main component of natural gas.

clue.text: Escape taking one's seat

parts.note: a pilot bailing out of a jet is shot clear still strapped into the seat

explanation.surface: A getaway in which you take your seat with you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking one's seat' sounds like sitting down, but the seat leaves the aircraft with the pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: To bail out of an aircraft by ejector seat is to be shot out, seat and all.

clue.text: Rare book

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare book' reads as a collector's item, but the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel means new and unusual, so rare; a novel is also a full-length work of fiction.

clue.text: Film recorded in foreign city (not Monte)

indicators.note: not Monte means those letters are removed from the city

parts.note: Montevideo is the capital of Uruguay
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A film shot abroad, but not in Monte Carlo.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not Monte)' looks like a hint away from Monte Carlo, but it removes MONTE from MONTEVIDEO.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorded film on tape or digital media is a video.

clue.text: A device for drawing — tie-breaker needed?

definitions.text: A device for drawing — tie-breaker needed?

parts.words: A device for drawing — tie-breaker needed?
parts.note: a technical drawing instrument, and a tennis game level at six all whose winner must be decided by a tiebreak

explanation.surface: A drawing instrument, and a drawn tennis game that needs settling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' means sketching, but in tennis a drawn set at six games all is settled by a tiebreak.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangular drafting tool for ruling angles, also readable as a tennis set left level.

clue.text: Loner is made to join up

indicators.note: loner is made into something else, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A solitary person is forced to enlist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is made' reads as compulsion, but it signals rearranging LONER.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up as a member, enlist, or register.

clue.text: Codicils and dead letters

indicators.note: the letters of the words and dead are what make the answer, rearranged

explanation.surface: Additions to a will, and the letters of someone who has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead letters' looks like undeliverable post, but 'letters' tells you to rearrange the letters of 'and dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Codicils are supplements added to a will, and addenda are additions to a document.

clue.text: A plug or notice applicable to gold

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
apt means suitable, applicable
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A plug or an advertisement relevant to gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A plug' looks like a promotion (as is 'notice'), but it is the electrical fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical fitting that lets one kind of plug connect to a different socket.

clue.text: It is necessary to do or die to gain entry here

indicators.note: only the part of the following three-word phrase that is needed is kept: its opening run of letters

explanation.surface: A desperate do-or-die effort is the only way to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do or die' sounds like a desperate effort, but only the run of letters in 'do or' is needed; 'die' is surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged panel is the usual way of getting into a room or building.

clue.text: Bowdlerise in crayon?

explanation.walkthrough: Bowdlerise means to censor prudishly, after Thomas Bowdler's expurgated Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors censored text with a coloured pencil, so to blue-pencil is to cut; literally a blue crayon.
